title: Overload protection dashboards and alerting spec (Hosted API canary)
author: Aisha Bello
body:
## Purpose
This spec defines the dashboards and alert thresholds for operating **Hosted overload protection** (circuit breakers + load shedding) along the request path (gateway → routing → runtime) during the canary rollout.

Goals:
- Catch overload before tail latency and timeouts climb.
- Make breaker and shedding behavior visible and safe to tune.
- Give incident responders one “what’s happening?” view with runbook links.
- Keep **metric cardinality bounded** and alerts actionable (no paging on expected, controlled shedding).

Non-goals:
- Policy design details (see policy engine integration doc).
- Per-tenant dashboards (only for targeted investigations; default views are tier/region/model).

## Audience
- SRE oncall, Platform oncall (gateway/policy), Smart Routing oncall, Serving Runtime oncall
- Support/CS (read-only) for interpreting overload errors and correlation IDs

## Dashboard stack + conventions
- Platform: Grafana + Prometheus (Telemetry Platform)
- Sources: gateway, routing and runtime saturation metrics plus SLO-toolkit classification
- All dashboards default to UTC
- Required variables on every dashboard: `region` (`us-east`, `us-west`, `eu-central`), `tier` (`hosted_self_serve`, `hosted_enterprise`, `dedicated`), `route` (`chat.completions`, `embeddings`, `rerank`), `model` (canonical ID, e.g. `rw-llama-3-70b`)

Cardinality rules:
- No raw `tenant_id` or `api_key` labels by default.
- Tenant drilldown lives on a separate short-retention “debug” dashboard.
- Bucket prompt length and token counts (`prompt_tokens_bucket`, `max_tokens_bucket`).

## Dashboard set (required)
### 1) Executive overview: “Overload protection — Control plane & serving health”
For incident triage; readable in 5 minutes.
1. **Availability + latency**: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency by route; error rate split into `2xx`, `4xx`, `5xx`, `overload` (ADR-014); timeouts.
2. **Breaker and shedding summary**: breaker opens/min by layer; shed rate by reason; Retry-After presence rate.
3. **Capacity/saturation**: runtime prefill/decode queue depth; token/sec saturation ratio; KV cache pressure.
4. **Top contributors**: regions by shed rate, models by breaker opens, routes by overload errors.

### 2) Breakers deep dive: “Circuit breakers — state, reasons, and policy outcomes”
- Breaker state timeline (Closed → Open → Half-open) by `breaker_name` and `region`
- Open reasons (stacked): `gpu_queue_depth_high`, `scheduler_backlog_high`, `token_saturation_high`, `memory_pressure_high`, `dependency_unhealthy`, `regional_capacity_low`, `policy_manual_override`
- Policy evaluation: rule match share, evaluation latency (p50/p95), policy engine errors
- Annotations: config deploys and canary toggles

### 3) Load shedding outcomes: “Admission control — shed/degrade/fallback breakdown”
- Outcomes (stacked): `admitted`, `shed`, `degraded`, `fallback_routed`
- Shed by HTTP status (`429`, `503`) and overload error code
- Fallback attempt and success rate; loop prevention counters
- Streaming: stream concurrency cap hit rate; early stream termination rate

### 4) Runtime saturation: “Serving runtime — queues, throughput, and memory pressure”
- Prefill and decode queue depth (gauge + p95 across pods)
- Admission wait time
- Token/sec by model family; saturation ratio
- KV cache occupancy and eviction rate; OOM/alloc failure rate
- Aggregate at `model + region` with bounded pod labels.

### 5) Customer experience: “Overload errors — semantics, headers, and correlation”
- Overload responses by error code
- Retry-After distribution (p50/p95 seconds)
- Correlation ID presence rate
- Retry storm indicators (inbound vs admitted amplification)

## Standard metric definitions (canonical)
### Gateway / control plane
- `gateway_requests_total{route,region,tier,code}`
- `gateway_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route,region,tier}`
- `gateway_overload_actions_total{action,reason,route,region,tier}` with `action ∈ {shed,degrade,admit}`
- `gateway_breaker_state{breaker_name,region}` (0=closed,1=open,2=half_open)
- `gateway_breaker_open_total{breaker_name,reason,region}`
- `gateway_retry_after_set_total{route,region,tier}`

### Routing
- `routing_fallback_attempts_total{from_model,to_model,region,tier}`
- `routing_fallback_success_total{from_model,to_model,region,tier}`
- `routing_loop_prevention_total{reason,region}`
- `routing_policy_eval_errors_total{region}`

### Runtime
- `runtime_queue_depth{queue,model,region}` (`queue ∈ {prefill,decode}`)
- `runtime_admission_wait_seconds_bucket{model,region}`
- `runtime_tokens_per_second{model,region,phase}`
- `runtime_saturation_ratio{model,region}`
- `runtime_kv_cache_pressure{model,region}`
- `runtime_oom_total{model,region}`

### SLO classification (slo-toolkit)
- `api_errors_total{class,route,region,tier}` with `class ∈ {success,customer_error,server_error,overload}`

## Recommended alerting philosophy
1. **Page on unexpected failure, not controlled shedding.** Correctly-signalled overload errors are a degradation mode; page only when shedding is sustained, misclassified, or caused by bugs.
2. **Multi-window burn rates** for customer-visible SLOs, paired with root-signal alerts.
3. **Symptom + cause pairing** (sustained overload plus runtime saturation).
4. **No per-tenant paging by default**; route tenant issues through Support/Jira.

## Alert thresholds (initial defaults)
Canary defaults; to be tuned per region/model once baselines exist.

Table: paging alerts (P1/P2)
| Alert | Severity | Condition (per region, unless noted) | Duration | Rationale / Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| High end-to-end error budget burn (Hosted API) | P1 | SLO burn rate > 14x (5m) AND > 2x (1h) | immediate | Standard multi-window burn using SLO-toolkit classification. |
| Sustained overload shed rate high | P1 | `shed / (admitted + shed) > 5% (all hosted tiers)` | 10m | Single threshold during canary. |
| Policy engine errors | P1 | `policy_eval_errors_total` > 1% of requests OR sustained 5xx from policy service | 5m | Policy engine errors amplify outages. |
| Runtime queue depth critical | P1 | `runtime_queue_depth{queue=decode} > critical_threshold` (per model family) | 10m | Decode backlog drives tail latency/timeouts. |
| Runtime OOM spike | P1 | `runtime_oom_total` increases > 5 in 15m for a model/region | 15m | OOMs tend to cascade. |

Table: ticket alerts (non-paging)
| Alert | Action | Condition | Duration | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| Overload errors trending up | Ticket | overload class errors > baseline + 2σ | 30m | Threshold tuning during rollout. |
| Increased stream cap hits | Ticket | stream cap hit rate > 2% | 30m | Can be expected during bursts. |
| Correlation ID missing | Ticket | correlation ID present rate < 99.5% | 30m | Debuggability regression. |

## Per-tier guidance
- hosted_enterprise: prefer graceful degradation (fallback routing) over raw shedding; expect low sustained shed.
- hosted_self_serve: prefer predictable shedding with clear errors over timeouts.
- dedicated: protections mainly enforce tenant isolation and protect the control plane; fix saturation with capacity.

## Required annotations and runbook links
- Pinned links: “Hosted overload circuit breaker runbook”, “Runtime overload mitigation runbook”, “Overload error taxonomy (ADR-014)”, “Admission control layering (ADR-015)”
- Annotations: overload policy config deploys, rollout toggles / canary flags

## Example PromQL snippets (reference)
Shed rate (per region, tier):
- sum(rate(gateway_overload_actions_total{action="shed",region=~"$region",tier=~"$tier"}[5m]))
  / sum(rate(gateway_overload_actions_total{action=~"admit|shed",region=~"$region",tier=~"$tier"}[5m]))

Breaker open rate:
- sum(rate(gateway_breaker_open_total{region=~"$region"}[5m])) by (breaker_name, reason)

Runtime decode queue depth:
- quantile_over_time(0.95, runtime_queue_depth{queue="decode",region=~"$region"}[5m])

## Operational checklist (canary readiness)
- [ ] Executive overview live for each canary region
- [ ] Breaker deep dive has policy-change annotations
- [ ] Alerts wired to #eng-oncall with correct paging routes
- [ ] Runbook links accessible to Support (read-only)
- [ ] Cardinality review done (no tenant_id on default dashboards)
- [ ] Thresholds checked against the perf-canary burst scenario

## Owners and escalation
Primary owner (dashboards/alerts): **Aisha Bello (Eng SRE)**
- Breaker/policy issues: Ethan Park / Jordan Lee
- Routing fallback issues: Mina Haddad / Elena Popov
- Runtime saturation: Sofia Ivanova / Omar El-Sayed
- Telemetry platform: Logan Wright

## Change management
- Paging threshold changes need a PR to observability-pack alert rules, review from Eng SRE plus the subsystem owner, and a note in #eng-oncall.

## Changelog
- 2025-10-20: Added runtime OOM alert and stream cap ticket alert.
- 2025-09-15: Initial canary spec (executive overview + breaker deep dive).
